items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: She was involved with Gray Gordon, with Blue Baron, owned a piece of the band in return for putting them in there and putting us in there, you know, for the air time, and she got a cut off the top until the union stopped it.

ctx.x: Well, true, but who is he handling? He's handling ghost bands, the Glenn Miller Band, the Jimmy Dorsey Band, the Tommy Dorsey Band. Well, he's got Kenton and he's got Maynard Ferguson and Woody Herman. But where are the new bands, Pat? Where are they? There aren't any new bands. And this is the whole thing. I mean it's almost impossible today for a new band to get started. You could say Buddy Rich is a new band if you want to. But Buddy Rich is not a new band. Buddy Rich is an old name which a band was built…

making it, or bands, let's put it that way, then you might say there might be a resurgence in the band business. Although I can't see economically where they could possibly make it. Even in our time there were angels. Maria Kramer at the Lincoln-Edison Hotel. She -- well, we were involved in a deal. She was involved with Jan Savitt. She was involved with Gray Gordon, with Blue Baron, owned a piece of the band in return for putting them in there and putting us in there, you know, for the air time, and she got a…

arrangement. There's no way in the world that a new band can overcome those costs. That's why I say there will never be the big band business. Now when we -- God forbid -- when we lose the guys that are still out on the road, the names of anybody that is left there, there won't be any names left, and then where is your big band business? Willard is trading on what happened before. He's not trading on anything new. Period. I rest my case.
